setup: Lie with your eyes under the bar
Feet flat, glutes and upper back on the bench
Grip a little wider than your shoulders
Pull your shoulder blades back and down
execution: Unrack and set the bar over your shoulders
Lower to your lower chest, forearms vertical
Press up and back to over your shoulders
faults: Don't bounce the bar off your chest
Don't lift your hips off the bench
Don't let your shoulders roll forward at lockout
Don't let your wrists bend far back

notes: Bench in a rack or bench station with safety arms set just below your chest at the bottom of the rep, or with a spotter. Don't bench heavy alone without either.
A bar trapped on the chest or neck is rare but has caused deaths. Safety arms or a spotter prevent it.
Wrap your thumbs around the bar. Avoid a thumbless grip.
If you use a spotter, agree the lift-off, the rep count and the help signal before the set.
Very wide grips raised modelled shoulder load in one small study. A grip a little wider than the shoulders is a sensible default.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Push-up
regressions.reason: Same pressing pattern, scalable, with no bar to get stuck under.

regressions.name: Chest press machine
regressions.reason: Guided path; safe to train hard alone.

progressions.name: Paused bench press
progressions.reason: A short pause on the chest builds control and strength off the chest.

progressions.name: Close-grip bench press
progressions.reason: A narrower grip shifts more work to the triceps.

substitutions.name: Dumbbell bench press
substitutions.reason: Same pattern; each arm works on its own and the weights can be lowered to the sides. Load is each dumbbell.

substitutions.name: Chest press machine
substitutions.reason: Guided path; no spotter needed. Stack numbers are not comparable.

substitutions.name: Incline bench press
substitutions.reason: Same bar and grip; more upper chest and front shoulder.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view, head on the left, bench along the floor line, camera at bench height. Uprights optional, drawn behind the figure.

keyPositions.label: Start
keyPositions.describe: Lying on a flat bench with head, upper back and glutes on the pad and a small upper-back arch. Feet flat on the floor, knees bent about 90°. Arms straight and vertical, bar directly over the shoulder joints.

keyPositions.label: Halfway
keyPositions.describe: Bar halfway down, drifting slightly toward the lower chest. Elbows bending, forearms close to vertical under the bar.

keyPositions.label: Chest touch
keyPositions.describe: Bar lightly touching the lower chest, around the nipple line or just below. Forearms close to vertical, wrists stacked over the elbows. Elbows slightly below the torso line. Upper back, glutes and feet still planted.

guideBrief.barPath: Slight diagonal from over the shoulders down to the lower chest and back; horizontal travel roughly 4–8% of body height
emphasise: Bar touches the lower chest and finishes over the shoulders
Forearms near vertical at the bottom
Feet, glutes and upper back stay planted

uncertain.note: The horizontal bar travel (4–8% of height) is an estimate, not from a cited measurement. Touch point varies with grip and arch.
Approximate drawing targets. Shoulder angles are the side-view projection; the elbows also move out to the side, which a side view can't show.
